Neurosurgery · published research

Spinal cord injury

A small multicenter human RCT reported faster early motor recovery, with between-group differences not persisting at 6 and 12 months.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A small multicenter human RCT reported faster early motor recovery, with between-group differences not persisting at 6 and 12 months.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact spinal-cord category contains 68 unique titles. It includes 51 animal-tagged publications, six human clinical reports, and 11 reviews or syntheses. In-vitro tags occur within nine animal-tagged records and are not nine additional cohorts. The recent multicenter human trial is a distinct clinical study, not a review or animal experiment. (Liang et al. 2026)

Human and clinical evidence

Four randomized human reports, one single-arm study, and one case series are indexed. The multicenter trial randomized 66 patients with incomplete acute cervical injury; 56 completed 12-month follow-up. PBM was associated with higher motor scores at early assessments, but between-group differences were not significant at six or 12 months. All participants received decompression surgery, so the evidence concerns PBM as an adjunct to acute care.

Animal evidence

The 51 animal-tagged records include 41 rat studies, nine mouse studies, and one miniature-pig study. Many test spinal-cord injury models and report functional or histologic outcomes. These experiments provide biological rationale but cannot establish clinical effectiveness, functional recovery, or safety in people.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

Nine records carry an in-vitro tag, all overlapping animal-tagged publications in the database. Cell or tissue outcomes therefore should not be added to the animal-publication count as independent studies.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The preclinical studies use varied red and near-infrared wavelengths, doses, timing, and injury models. Human regimens and co-interventions also vary. The database does not support one transferable dose or schedule, and it does not justify inferring human settings from animal protocols.

Interpretation

The recent clinical signal supports a larger confirmatory trial, particularly for early motor recovery. Small human samples, attrition, adjunctive surgery, and convergence of long-term outcomes limit claims of durable benefit. Future studies should standardize rehabilitation, stratify injury severity, and measure motor scores, independent ambulation, function, pain, and adverse events through longer follow-up.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact category includes 68 unique titles, but most are animal studies or secondary reviews and only a few are human clinical publications. A recent multicenter trial reported early motor-recovery gains, while between-group differences were not sustained at 6 or 12 months. Further trials need replication, fuller safety reporting, and standardized rehabilitation.
